root_cause.text: The MMCID exit code incorrectly assumed that a task in per-CPU mode always has a CPU-owned CID (ONCPU bit set), but a race condition can leave the MM_CID_TRANSIT bit set without ONCPU, causing mm_drop_cid_on_cpu() to treat the TRANSIT bit as a CID index and perform an out-of-bounds clear_bit().
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: "sched_mm_cid_exit() assumes that the CID is CPU owned because the prior mode was per CPU. It invokes mm_drop_cid_on_cpu() which clears the not set ONCPU bit and then invokes clear_bit() with an insanely large bit number because TRANSIT is set (bit 29)." The patch adds a `if (cid_on_cpu(pcp->cid))` guard in `mm_drop_cid_on_cpu()` to validate CPU ownership before clearing.

intent_record.what: Updated the comment inside sched_mm_cid_exit to clarify that the TRANSIT bit may have been set and handled, and that the CID is dropped if owned by the CPU.
intent_record.how: No runtime behavior change; only a comment update for improved accuracy and clarity.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add guard to only clear and drop CID if the ONCPU bit is set.
intent_record.what: Added a conditional check (cid_on_cpu(pcp->cid)) before clearing the ONCPU bit and calling mm_drop_cid() in mm_drop_cid_on_cpu().
intent_record.how: The function now only removes the ONCPU state from the per-CPU CID storage and drops the CID from the mm's tracking if the CID actually has the ONCPU bit set, avoiding extraneous operations when the bit is already clear.

relevance_review.reason: The change only clarifies a comment in sched_mm_cid_exit without modifying any code logic. The vulnerability root cause involves a race condition and an incorrect assumption leading to an out-of-bounds clear_bit() operation, which is not directly addressed by comment clarification.

The group's change directly addresses the root cause by adding a guard to check the ONCPU bit before clearing the CID, preventing the out-of-bounds operation that occurs when the condition is not met.

candidates.rationale: This assignment extracts the CID from pcp->cid without checking the ONCPU bit. If the MM_CID_TRANSIT bit is set without ONCPU, cpu_cid_to_cid may treat the TRANSIT bit as part of the CID index, producing an out-of-bounds value.

This call uses the potentially invalid CID (obtained from the previous assignment) to drop the CID, which performs an out-of-bounds clear_bit() due to the TRANSIT bit being interpreted as a CID index.
